first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and simplifying onboarding is the only candidate direction directly positioned to address both leading indicators while supporting durable self-serve revenue. Verify memory_86 because it is central to this choice and its underlying evidence is archived; verify memory_73 because competitor pricing makes promotional pricing a consequential alternative, but its long-term revenue trade-offs need scrutiny before displacing a product-led intervention.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly addresses both current declines: onboarding completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. This supports sustainable qualified revenue more credibly than promotional pricing, whose verified 18% qualified-revenue lift was paired with 12% lower 30-day retention and failure to survive the first renewal cycle. Signup simplification also independently supports an SMB activation benefit.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified evidence shows it improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, addressing the current activation and completion deterioration with a durable value mechanism. The new pricing pressure raises urgency, but the only pricing evidence shows targeted discounting increases short-term signups and qualified revenue while reducing 30-day retention by 12% and failing before renewal; a deeper competitive discount is therefore a material downstream-value risk, not a sustainable-response experiment.
